title: Bundle variables, targets and overrides for dev, test and prod
objective_text: Use bundle variables, targets and overrides to promote one codebase across dev, test and prod.
scenario: The orders pipeline's bundle deploys the same job to three workspaces. Last week a deploy with no -t went to prod, test wrote into the dev catalog, and the prod job ran as an engineer who has since left. Fix the bundle so one codebase promotes cleanly.
engine_label: A model of a bundle's databricks.yml, checked on this PC
verifies: Your bundle settings send each target to its own catalog through one variable, make dev the default in development mode, and protect prod with production mode, a Git branch and a service principal, as the bundle docs describe, checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That the bundle validates or deploys: the Databricks CLI doesn't run here, and the file is JSON, not YAML.
Variable precedence from --var, BUNDLE_VAR_ environment variables or variable-overrides.json, or lookups.

expected.description: The job's catalog is ${var.catalog}; test and prod override it; dev is the only default and runs in development mode; prod is production mode, branch main, run as the kf-deployer service principal.

validation.pass: One codebase, one variable: each target says which catalog it writes to.
validation.fail: A target writes to the wrong catalog.

rules.why: A catalog written into the job deploys the same value to every target; ${var.catalog} takes each target's value.
Without a test value, test gets the default, dev.

validation.pass: dev is the default target, in development mode.
validation.fail: A deploy with no -t doesn't go where it should.

rules.why: With dev as the default, databricks bundle deploy with no -t goes to dev.
Development mode prefixes resource names and pauses schedules and triggers.
Only one target can be the default.
Only one target can be the default, and prod should need -t prod.

validation.pass: prod deploys only from main, in production mode, as the service principal.
validation.fail: prod isn't protected the way production needs.

rules.why: In production mode the CLI checks that the current Git branch is the target's branch.
Databricks recommends service principals for production deployments; run_as takes the service principal's application ID.

explanation: Write the setting that changes between environments once, as a variable, and read it with ${var.catalog}; each target then overrides the value in its own variables mapping, and the top-level default covers dev. Only one target may be the default, and it should be dev, so a deploy without -t can't reach prod. Development mode prefixes names and pauses schedules; production mode checks the Git branch, and running as a service principal keeps the prod job from depending on one person's account.
hints: A literal "prod" in the job's parameter is the same in every target. Replace it with ${var.catalog}.
A target's variables mapping overrides the variable for that target: targets.test.variables.catalog.
One and only one target can be default: true.
Production mode with git.branch main refuses a deploy from another branch; run_as.service_principal_name runs the job as the service principal.
